next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added two generalized permissive rules — marking candidate boundaries after topic/subject/object/locative-marked noun phrases even before their governing predicate appears, and after short adverbial/temporal/quantity phrases — to increase the pool of defensible fine-grained boundaries so small-T budgets (e.g. T=3) are not starved of candidates (addresses coverage/truncation_shortfall).

[Examples — Segment]: Replaced one redundant -고-connective example with a new example illustrating a boundary after a topic-marked noun phrase preceding its predicate, to demonstrate the new permissive rule without exceeding the 12-example cap.

next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added a new permissive rule distinct from the previously-rejected single-topic-NP rule: mark a boundary after each item in a coordinate/enumerated list of nouns or short clauses joined by -이랑/-랑/-하고/-도 or commas, even before the shared governing predicate appears, since each listed item is independently renderable. This increases the pool of low-risk fine-grained candidates for small-T budgets without touching the earlier (rejected) NP-before-predicate rule.

[Examples — Segment]: Removed a redundant -고-connective example (연봉도 괜찮고/워라밸도 좋다고) and replaced it with a new example illustrating the coordinate-list rule, keeping the example count at 10 (under the 12 cap) while demonstrating the new rule.

next_changelog: [When to Segment]: Added a rule that when a clause-chaining connective is followed later by a governing verb that fixes reported speech, obligation, or habitual aspect for the whole chain (e.g. -라고 하다, -해야 되다, -게 되다), the safer boundary is AFTER that governing verb, not right after the earlier connective — addresses placement failures where tense/modality/actor-role was asserted early and then contradicted.

[Never Segment]: Added three generalized restrictions: (1) do not close a boundary right after a connective clause when a later reported-speech/obligation/habitual governing verb has not yet appeared, (2) do not separate a subject-marking particle from a later collective/pronominal noun phrase that depends on it for an inclusive reading, (3) do not close a boundary right after a subject-omitted converbal clause when no subject has been introduced yet in the sentence — these target the four placement failures (wrong tense fixed early, wrong actor role, lost antecedent, invented subject) without reducing overall boundary generosity elsewhere.
